comparison: Perfect agreement on testis-specific expression claims (C2, C36-C42, C44-C46). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED using multiple complementary approaches (qPCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, phylogenetic analysis). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the conclusive nature of the expression data.

Strong agreement on knockout validation and male-specific sterility (C47-C51). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes rescue experiment validation (C56), while peer review focuses on the novelty of the first FBXO24 KO mouse model. Peer review R2 covers only C47-C51, while OpenEval R2 includes additional histological claims.

Both address histological defects in spermatogenesis (C52-C57). OpenEval R2 and peer R3 both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note small but significant reductions in testis size and spermatogenic cells. The rescue experiment is accepted without critique by peer reviewers.

Strong agreement on flagellar structural defects documented by electron microscopy (C58-C67). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe this as 'a very strong point' with thorough documentation. Peer review notes missing quantification for some defects as a presentation issue, not a data quality concern.

Both address flagellar structural defects and their functional consequences (C68-C70). OpenEval R3 includes broader flagellar analysis, while peer R5 focuses specifically on mitochondrial sheath and outer dense fiber defects. Both rate as SUPPORTED and accept the causal link to reduced motility.

Both address protein level changes in flagellar components (C71, C72, C74). OpenEval R3 and peer R6 both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the data as reliable observations but note mechanistic interpretation questions about ubiquitination involvement.

Both address the causal role in sperm motility (C75-C76). OpenEval R3 notes this inference is 'reasonable but somewhat speculative,' while peer R7 rates as SUPPORTED and affirms the causal role. Slight difference in confidence level regarding mechanistic certainty.

Strong agreement on mitochondrial defects, CB enlargement, and MIWI protein increase (C77-C78, C81-C83). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe the MIWI finding as 'an important point' consistent with CB enlargement. Both note the specificity of MIWI increase while other CB proteins remain unchanged.

Agreement on sperm head defects and nuclear condensation issues (C84-C88). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes SEM and TEM documentation, while peer reviewers confirm careful characterization of chromatin defects during spermiogenesis.

Strong agreement on histone-protamine transition defects (C90-C93, C95). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm increased histones/transition proteins and reduced protamines, consistent with less condensed nuclei. Both accept the lack of direct histone interaction (C92).

Agreement on RNA-seq data showing large-scale transcriptomic changes (C96-C106). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes missing details on replicates and statistical methods. Peer reviewers accept the data as valid but note uncertainty about whether changes are direct or indirect consequences of FBXO24 loss.

Agreement on splicing factor interactions and altered splicing (C3, C108-C111, C113). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mechanism of splicing factor regulation is not fully elucidated. Peer reviewers accept interaction and splicing data but question whether ubiquitination involvement was demonstrated for splicing factors.

Agreement on FBXO24-MIWI protein interactions and domain mapping (C11-C12, C114-C116). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple IP approaches and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers confirm the finding is 'well supported with experiments performed in 293T cells.'

Strong agreement on ubiquitination mechanism with K48-linkage specificity (C13, C117-C123). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers describe this as 'well supported' with both ectopic system and endogenous validation. Both accept K48 vs K63 specificity without challenge.

Agreement on piRNA changes but divergence on interpretation (C14-C15, C124-C135). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes lack of replicates/normalization details and need for causal validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, accepting the data but questioning functional significance and contribution to infertility phenotype.

Agreement on overall dual mechanism conclusion (C4-C5, C16, C136, C166-C167). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes relative contributions not quantified and some inferential steps. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, describing it as 'solid work' and 'important study,' but note mechanistic narrative gaps regarding E3 ubiquitin ligase role.

OpenEval R11 addresses literature-based contextual claims (C17-C35) establishing background and knowledge gaps. Rated as SUPPORTED with note to verify citation accuracy. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses cited literature claims providing context (C73, C79-C80, C89, C94, C101, C112, C138-C144, C152-C157, C159-C162). Rated as SUPPORTED but notes inconsistency between C140 and C94 regarding RNF8. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature citations.

OpenEval R13 addresses interpretive and speculative claims (C137, C141-C142, C145-C151, C158, C163-C165). Rated as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable inferences but speculation beyond direct data support, particularly regarding piRNA transcriptional repression (C163) and 'vicious circle' of aberrant splicing (C151). Peer review R16 touches on C158 but no comprehensive peer evaluation of these interpretive claims.
